instructor: He was very kind towards students and he was open for questions and communication. There were too many subjects. Because there were so many topics and we started late, we went through the lessons quickly, and I found it difficult to follow.
Our teacher showed an extremely sensitive and understanding approach towards his students.

Peter Hoca is a great person, he is always so kind and helpful. He speaks fast sometimes, which makes it hard to catch him. It is clear that he is very ambitious in his field. He could be more generous while grading.
Prof Talloen is incredibly knowledgable and replies to all questions very quickly and provides us with plenty of additional reading material.

Strongest: he is very passionate about the course he explain everything really well. 

Weakest: 
He marks assignments a little too hard

Professor Talloen is a very nice person who does his job well and has good communication with his students. However, since he spoke very fast during his lectures, I often got distracted from the lesson. Although I liked his slides and the information he gave during the lesson, he could not provide interaction during the lesson, which resulted in students losing their attention during the lesson. The issue of grades is a completely different issue, he is a person who has a very strict grading system in his mind, if you do not give the same answer he wants, he deducts points. He also has not accepted close answers most of the time. Although I like him very much as a person, I can say that this lesson period was not productive for me.

Strongest: He could manage the time to finish all the topics on time, even though there were classes cancelled due to his busy programme at Sagalassos excavation site. He is someone so kind and helpful, answers your questions directly on point any time. He is an excellent person and professor for Archeology students. I am not an archeology student and was not very succesful in this field but happy to take the class from him.  

There is no weakest points about him:)
course: Course is good, no complaints

This is a loaded course, there is a lot to teach and learn, so we had to be fast sometimes. I learned a lot in the course. But if you are going to take the course as an elective, you should be careful, it might be challenging for you, especially if you are not that interested in the course topic.

I think the course could have benefitted from a little more about the social and cultural aspects of Ancient Greece such as customs and gender roles, festivals etc. The course focuses a lot on architecture and material culture

This course might not be a good idea to take as an elective in the last year for POLS students if you are not familiar with Greek Archeology. You need to find enough time to put effort to learn and repeat the slides. Slides are long (average 100 pages per week) if I compare with POLS department courses. HOWEVER, I think this course is excellent if you are interested in greek and ancient architecture, and perfect for people who like to pay attention to details of things. There were bunch of beautiful and meaningful details of temples, walls, bottles, vases, paintings... You can take this course as an elective in a semester which is not busy. Then, you will definitely learn many things about Greek culture, ancient human history from items and buildings, sculptures, paintings...(if you have 4-5 courses for instance).

It is a very intense course. There were too many slides. It was overwhelming. I had difficulty studying for the final exam, and instead of fundamental topics, there were details on the exam. There could have been more questions instead of just four, given that there were so many topics.
I think the foundation of archaeology was laid with this course.

instructor: He is the greatest instructor ever! No weakest points

I think the amount of knowledge Peter Hoca has is astounding, and it is very apparent. He covered the course content in a comprehensive way. I think perhaps a bit more interaction with the class might have improved the course and made it more engaging. Additionally, I think perhaps better communication (especially with the non-HART-major students) might have helped as we came to class for a period that Peter Hoca wasn't coming and weren't notified by the department administrative assistant like the major students were.

Peter Hoca iletişime geçmesi kolay ve karşılıklı saygı ve anlayış çerçevesinde konuşabileceğiniz, soru sorulduğunda sıkılmadan sabırla yanıtlayan biri, öğrencileriyle sağladığı saygı çerçevesinde ama yine de samimi hissettiren iletişimi beğeniyorum.. Ders notları/slaytları fazlasıyla açıklayıcı, bir öğrencinin ihtiyacı olan optimal bilgi ve görsele sahip notlar paylaşıyor ve slaytlarını sisteme yüklemekte de çok gecikmiyor.  Ancak kendisinin ders anlatış şekli karşıdakiniin anlamasına el verişli değil. Derste sınıfın en uzak köşesine geçip sınıfa sırtını dönüp tahtaya bakarak ders anlatıyor. Çok hızlı konuştuğu için ağzını okumaya çalışıyoruz ama sırtı bize dönük olduğu için çoğu zaman ağzından çıkan uğultulu kelimeleri anlayamıyoruz. Dersinde kelimelerini hızlı kullanmasının yanı sıra yarın yokmuşçasına konuları hızlı bir şekilde anlatıyor. 20 saniye zone out olduğunuzda minimum1-2 slayt kaçırmış oluyorsunuz bu kadar hızlı konuşmasıyla; ki hızlı konuştğu için ve aktif olarak dediklerini anlamakta zorlandığımız için zone out yaşama ihtimali daha da artıyor. Aynı zamanda kendisinin sınavlarda soru sorma/ notlandırma şeklini de efektif bulduğumu söyleyemem. Yoruma ve farklı bakış açılarına hiç açık olmayan, sadece ezbere dayalı bir soru sorma şekli var. Kendi kafasında bir soruya madde madde cevap oluşturuyor ve bu maddelerden birini eksik yazarsan puan kırıyor.
course: It was a very useful and beneficial course

Dersin içeriğinde çok önemli, eğlenmesi çok keyifli bilgiler varken Peter Hoca içeriği çok tekdüzeleştiriyor. Hem quizlerde hem mt/final sınavlarında eleştirel yorum yapabileceğimiz, akademik anlamda kendimizi geliştirebileceğimiz  bir ders olabilecekken Peter hoca'nın soru sorma biçimiyle beynimizi eleştirel ve analitik bir şekilde kullanmamıza gerek kalmayan, sadece "explain what this artifact is, situate in time and space, explain its importance" şeklinde sorularıyla bir yapının veya tarihi eserin nerde ne zamana tarihlendiğini bilmenin yeteceği bir öğretim sistemine dönmüş bir şekilde. Dönemin başında öğretilenleri yorum yaparak, eleştirel bir şekilde öğrenmeye çalıştığım bu derste mid-term'den sonra yüksek not almak için sadece zaman mekan ve ismini bilip ne işe yaradığına dair ufak bir fikrim olduğu zaman kısa bir ezberle, çok da bir şey öğrenmeden yüksek not alınabileneceğini fark ettim.
Some aspects/periods weren't as engaging as others but I don't think that could be rectified since we have to learn about them.

instructor: Strongest is his knowledge. Weakest is not having much interaction

To be perfectly honest, this semester was a disaster. I think Peter should watch videos of good instructors teaching, and tries to better himself as he is a very bad teacher. He has walls of text in his powerpoint presentations, usually taken directly from different sources and he reads off of them from the start of the class until the end with a monotone pitch. It is like listening to an audiobook with a very bad narrator. It is impossible to pay attention to him and scan through the presentation at the same time. I have asked him on the first week to upload these long presentations before class, which would allow us to take a look at them prior to class, so that I can pay attention to what he is saying during the lecture, but he rejected that outright. He has no interaction with students, no discussions, he just comes in to class, talks non-stop for 50-100 minutes and leaves. 
He has apologized for the incident that happened with the feedback of the first assignment, where he spent a whole class hour going over every students assignment by name on a powerpoint presentation and sometimes joking about our papers. However, there is a deeper problem with his attitude. He has stated that "he didn't fail anyone on this assignment and if we were attending his school in Belgium, all of our papers would have failed." I don't think he is aware of how bad of a statement this was. This is a 4th year course and we have been taught to write papers in this department for at least 3-4 years. He even suggested to me that I could have written my paper from one or two sources that is out there while this department prioritizes research from their students and bibliography is key to our assignments. With that statement he also implies unknowingly that our other instructors don't know how to read papers and grade them since most of us who took this class made it to our third or fourth year in this school and most probably some of us even got good grades from our previous papers.

Bence ( iyi niyetli de olsa) hepimizin paperlarına sınıfta toplu bir feedback vermek, isim isim slayt hazırlanması ve yalnızca yanlışların konuşulması çok rendice ediciydi. Ben karnıma daha çok ağrı giren bir derse girdiğimi hatırlamıyorum. Sonrasında destek olmaya çalışıp bizim için bir şeyleri kolaylaştırdı ancak yine de o dersi aşabilecek miyiz emin değilim.

Bu ders çok kötüydü. Dersi dinleyebilmek için bütün dönem boyunca çok çabaladım ama dikkatim hep çok dağıldı çünkü hoca çoğu wikiden olan slidelarda ne yazıyorsa onu okudu öğretmek yerine.  Bu takip etme açısından çok kötü ve zorlayıcı. Bizden hocalar sunum beklediklerinde sunuma her şeyi yazmamızı yüz defa söylerler. Bütün dönem böyle geçti sadece son iki hafta bir anda değişti. Yenisi çok daha iyi olsa da koskoca bir dönem hevesle başladığım dersi büyük hayal kırıklığıyla bitirmeme sebep oldu.  Hiç geri bildirim alamadık ta ki 11. Haftaya kadar. Aldığımız tek geri bildirim verdiğimiz neredeyse 5bin kelimelik essaydi. Bu ödev öğrencilik hayatımda verdiğim en uzun ödevdi ve bence gereksiz uzundu. Geribildirim yapılış şeklinin de son derece yanlış olduğunu düşünüyorum. Hoca herkesin adı ve soyadıyla alıntılar yaparak herkesin içinde hatalarımızı yüzümüze vurdu bunun için sunum hazırladı. Hiç böyle utanmamıştım, hem kendi adıma hem arkadaşlarım adına. Ben kimsenin ne yazdığını bilmek zorunda değildim. Bazı kişilerle dalga geçmesi, küçük görerek gülmesi, eşiyle beraber sohbet edip güldüklerini paylaşması, sürekli belçikada olsanız kalmıştınız demesi bence hem çok ayıp hem de çok kötüydü. Etik olarak da tüm bunların çok yanlış olduğunu düşünüyorum. Geribildirimlerin kendisine gelince, hiçbirinin yapıcı olduğunu düşünmüyorum. Eleştirilmek için eleştirildiğimiz hissini verdi. Bu kadar bibliographyye takılacaksa bize hangi formatta istediğini söylemeliydi biz de örneğin apa mi ona uyardık. Sınıftaki herkesin dersi çok ciddiye aldığını düşünüyorum. böyle bir sınıf olarak bir sınıf olarak bu kadar küçük görülmeyi ve düşük notları haketmedik. Hiçbirinizi bu essayden bırakmadım merak etmeyin anlayışlı davranıyorum tavrı da bence samimi değildi. Bütün bunlar yüzünden sözlüden önce çok gerildik ama sözlü korktuğumuzdan iyiydi.

Hoca bu sene okula geldi fakat okulu anlayıp bizi tanımak yerine kendi isteklerini bizim üzerimizde net olmayan bir şekilde uygulamaya çalıştı. Ders anlatışı iyi ve akıcı fakat ödev değerlendirmeleri, notlandırmalı feedback verişi çok düzensiz. Herkesin kağıdını sınıfta isim isim okuyarak feedback verdi.

It is obvious he is knowledgeable on the subject, but a lecturer needs to find a proper way to transfer that knowledge as well. Lessons were like info-dropping sessions with little to none dialogue, which gets exhausting after a while. It would be better to engage students into the subject by asking questions at the very least.
course: Öncelikle dersin slaytları o kadar tek düze ki oldukça zorlandım derse odaklanırken ve keşke daha az yazılı olsaydı böylece dersin içinde daha aktif olabilirdim. bu ders daha erken verilebilecek bir ders. çok fazla güzel şeyin öğrenebileceği ve bir bilkent arkeoloji öğrencisinin konuya hakim olması gereken bir ders. daha ilgi çekici hale gelirse güzel olacağını düşünüyorum.
It is a good core course that connects the bronze age to roman empire in anatolia.
Ders işleyiş olarak güzel ama sadece yerleşke işleniyor.

The format of oral exam as the final is the best aspect of the course, it was a bit risky but the teacher helped navigate the students answer.
The weakest aspect is the inconsistency between the course title and the course's content. It was very architecture oriented rather than aspects of daily life as indicated in the course title. Also, there are too many extra content that needs to be cut off in my opinion, almost half of the semester was spent on civilizations before Graeco-Roman periods. I wasn't expecting Phrygians or Hittites in this course, and they are not within the course's limits in my opinion. Either the syllabus needs to change, or the title of the course.

instructor: Whenever I needed help, he was there and open to help. Especially about 2 two papers we needed to write, he was supportive.

He knows a ton and expects everyone to know as much as he knows and I think it's impossible. A lifetime of experience and research cannot be taught in just 14 weeks and it's so unrealistic to expect the students to learn that in such a short period. I learned a lot, but the class took a great toll on me. Too much information just squeezed into 2 hours is torture. After each class I'd get headaches, started to think I might be stupid.
course: The course was very loaded. It covered a wide time period. We were constantly jumping to different topics and time periods without having time to digest. Besides the time period, it also covered lots of subtopics which needed to be focused on in more detail to understand the issue.  On the other hand, the lesson was only progressing through slides. We could not find the space to actively participate in the lesson. Due to the intensity of the topics, it was very difficult to listen with understanding while being a listener.

instructor: Mr. Talloen is a highly knowledgeable academic, yet I am not fond of how he lectures. I think the way he prefers is not really my style, I prefer more interactive classes. He speaks too fast and turns his back while he lectures, which makes it very hard to follow the class for me and I get easily distracted. I would prefer if he asks more questions and we had discussions in the class.
Peter hoca is great, you can learn a lot from him. Very kind and helpful person

Great personality. Funny, always smiles, respectful and helpful. Slides are full of information and always comes to the class prepared. He works in the field so you probably will not have anyone better than him to take this course. He was generous with the grading of presentations. Weakest point is that he never told us anything about format of presentation, midterm or anything likewise. I mean there was no prompt, other than the shallow conversations happening about them in class. If you missed that class, good luck. There is also this possibility of a communication medium existing between him and the rest of the class that I am not aware of because no one else in the class was bothered by this. How everybody knew not to come in the first week if he did not email us? Safe to say I questioned my sense of reality, I could have asked but did not maybe that is my fault. Anyways I would definitely take another course from him if offered.
course: ITS A LOADED COURSE: I ABSOLUTELY did NOT had the time to think about the presentation the instructor is talking about and form even a thought, let alone a question. The whooooooole semester felt like we are in a rush since the day one and it is tooooooo much information to digest to the point we do not learn anymore

I think this class could be better if we had more discussions in the classroom. There could be some extra readings and I think this way I could have actually learned more. Instead of having a midterm and a final, I think it would also make more sense for a fourth year class if we had more writing assignments about different topics. The topics are loaded and when I zone out for five minutes, I feel like I missed a lot. Yet, I think this class is very good in theory to actually combine what we have been learning the past four years.

instructor: One of the best instructors at Bilkent.

Peter Louis hocamız gerçekten alanına çok hakim birisi. Derse girdiğim zaman gerçekten, gerek Mezopotamya, gerek Mısır, Antik Yunan, Romalılar hakkında ve onlar tarafından yapılmış birçok eserler hakkında bilgiler edindim ve Peter Hoca öğrenme isteğime aşırı derecede katkıda bulundu. Onun anlatış stili ve bilgisi dersi keyifli kılıyor. Çok güzel bir İngilizcesi var, ve onun dışında Türkçeyi de çok iyi biliyor, kültürlü ve çok sempatik bir insan.
Dr. Talloen is approachable and nice

The only downside is that he focuses a little bit too much on slides, which lessens the interaction with the students. He could very well improve on this.  Other than that, he is a really knowledgeable and helpful instructor. You will most definitely love the insights and the details he will share. He is lenient and encouraging. It is really worth taking this course from him.

We could spend less time on prehistory to have time left for focusing on reneissance art. This class does offer the evolution of art in depth and, therefore, is more than impressive.

They were nice. Congratulations on the first-ever lecture. Nicely done.

instructor: From day 1 of this course, it was clear that it would be completely different experience. I learned tremendous amount in this course. I have to say that the weatlh of information he possesses and the detailed manner which he delivers this class was very valuable. This semester Peter hoca made a significant effort to include us in topics, encouraged us to ask questions. His teaching style was not just effective but I think was captivating as well. This course requires tons of readings, yet he managed to maintain our interest. I think this course is the most challenging one in undergraduate program in terms of its content. However he made the material comprehensible. I enjoyed preparing my presentations- both the discussion leading and my own topic. He was understanding and supportive. Thank you very much.
Peter Hoca is open to communication, and he always give advice those who seek it. Whenever I went to his room for any questions I had, he never rejected me
course: For a 4th year student in archaeology, introduction to theories and methods are really beneficial. The articles studied in the lesson are from the pioneer of the subject so it helps student to be familiarized with the concepts
